Kaplan-Meier life tables, as the ac job reports them

Source: R/life-table.R
life_table.Rd

The R counterpart of the SAS %KAPLAN macro, as the ac job calls it. life_table() returns the product-limit life table, overall or one per stratum. life_table_at() reads survival and the number at risk at reporting horizons, life_table_tests() compares strata, and life_table_keep() names the rows all three analyze, so a figure can be drawn over exactly the same patients.

Usage

life_table(
  data,
  time,
  event,
  strata = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.68268948,
  event_only = TRUE
)

life_table_at(
  data,
  time,
  event,
  times,
  labels = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.68268948
)

life_table_tests(data, time, event, strata)

life_table_keep(data, time, event, strata = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per patient.

time

Name of the follow-up time column.

event

Name of the event column, 0/1 or logical.

strata

Name of one stratification column, or NULL for the whole cohort.

conf_level

Confidence level of the limits. Default 0.68268948.

event_only

TRUE returns a row per event time only (SAS PEVENT=1); FALSE adds a row per censoring time (PEVENT=0).

times

Reporting horizons, in the unit of time.

labels

Labels for times. NULL labels each horizon with its value.

Value

life_table(): a data frame with the columns of TemporalHazard::hzr_kaplan() (time, n_risk, n_event, n_censor, survival, std_err, cl_lower, cl_upper, cumhaz, hazard, density, life), led by stratum when strata is given. Its attribute "counts" has a row per stratum with n, n_events, n_censored and max_fup, the last observed time; "dropped" is described under Details, or NULL.

life_table_at(): a data frame with a row per stratum and horizon: stratum when strata is given, then horizon, time, survival, cl_lower, cl_upper and n_risk, with the "dropped" attribute.

life_table_tests(): a data frame with a row per test: test, chisq, df and p_value, with the "dropped" attribute. A stratum with nobody at risk at any event time adds nothing to the log-rank or Wilcoxon test and is left out of its degrees of freedom.

life_table_keep(): a logical vector, TRUE for each analyzed row of data.

Details

Rows analyzed. A row is analyzed when its time and event are both recorded. With strata, a row whose stratum value is missing, or is a mean-imputed level (hvtiRutilities::imputed_levels()), is dropped too, as %KAPLAN drops "invalid strata values". The dropped rows are not silent: the result carries them in its "dropped" attribute, one row per reason, and the ac job prints that table.

Confidence level. The default conf_level is %KAPLAN's CLEVEL default, 0.68268948: one standard error, not 95%.

Reporting horizons. Survival at a horizon is the last estimate at or before it, and 1 before the first event. Beyond the last observation the estimate is not defined and is NA, unless survival has already reached zero. The number at risk is the number of patients whose time is greater than the horizon: the at-risk count on the first life-table row AFTER the horizon, when every censored time has a row (PEVENT=0). The estimate comes from the row before, the count from the row after.

Tests. life_table_tests() reports the three tests SAS PROC LIFETEST prints for strata: the log-rank, the Wilcoxon (Gehan's weights, the number at risk) and -2Log(LR), the likelihood ratio test of an exponential model. All three use every analyzed row to the end of follow-up. To compare curves only up to a horizon, censor the data there first, in the job.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("TemporalHazard", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d <- data.frame(
    years = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.9, 1.3, 2.0, 2.4, 3.1, 4.0, 5.5, 6.0),
    dead  = c(1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0),
    group = c("a", "b", "a", "b", "a", "b", "a", "b", "a", NA)
  )
  life_table(d, "years", "dead")
  life_table_at(d, "years", "dead", times = c(1, 2, 5), strata = "group")
  life_table_tests(d, "years", "dead", "group")
}
#>        test      chisq df   p_value
#> 1  Log-rank 0.31656099  1 0.5736817
#> 2  Wilcoxon 0.02173913  1 0.8827832
#> 3 -2Log(LR) 0.71392035  1 0.3981454
